changes.text: 原计划要宏大得多：横穿队伍立刻出发，踏上1800英里的行程，希望在五个月内穿越极点，抵达罗斯海一侧的基地。船被压毁之后，任务换成了另一件事——让全队上岸。

The plan he began with was far grander: "the Transcontinental party will set out on their 1800-mile journey at once," he wrote, "in the hope of accomplishing the march across the Pole and reaching the Ross Sea base in five months." Once the ice had crushed the ship, the task became something else entirely: get the whole party onto land.
在被他们称为抛弃营的地方，装备经历了一次大幅筛选。他决定给每人发一整套全新的 Burberrys 和内衣，再加新袜子；他还定下规矩：个人物品不得超过两磅，除了最必需的东西，一律不上路。照他的说法，他们负担不起多余的重量。

At a place they named Dump Camp, the equipment went through a severe weeding-out. He decided to issue each man a complete new set of Burberrys and underclothing, along with a supply of new socks. He also fixed the rule: "personal gear must not exceed two pounds per man," which meant nothing but bare necessaries would go on the march. As he put it, they could not afford to cumber themselves with unnecessary weight.
开路时有过顺利的时候。两组狗拉着小艇出发，只需帮一次手；他写道，十四条狗干得和十八个人一样好，甚至更好。十二个人用镐和铲，十分钟就能在一道约14英尺高的冰脊上凿出一条还算平整的路。

At one stage the work went well. Two dog teams were hitched to the cutter and "started off in splendid style. They needed to be helped only once; indeed fourteen dogs did as well or even better than eighteen men." A dozen men with picks and shovels could cut a road through a ridge about 14 feet high in ten minutes and leave a smooth, or comparatively smooth, path behind them.
他记下挪动两条船的艰难。雪面糟透了，他们从没见过这样的冰面：人有时陷到齐臀深，到处的雪都有两英尺厚。

He recorded how hard it was to shift the two boats. The surface was terrible, like nothing any of them had seen before: "We were sinking at times up to our hips, and everywhere the snow was two feet deep."
他还决定尽量省下宝贵的雪橇口粮，留给那趟必然要来的小艇航行，平时几乎全靠海豹和企鹅过活。他派人回抛弃营搜罗衣物、烟草之类，可几天大雪，加上融化下陷，留在那里的许多东西已经不见了。

He also decided, in his words, "to conserve our valuable sledging rations, which would be so necessary for the inevitable boat journey, as much as possible, and to subsist almost entirely on seals and penguins." A party went back to Dump Camp for clothing, tobacco and whatever else they could find, but heavy snow and the thaw had swallowed a good many of the things left there.
一种解释是（作者推断），海洋营不是他第一次决定停下。行军第二天早上，雪大得看不清路，他就决定不拔营；天晴一些后探到一块好走的浮冰，午饭后又继续走。两次决定看的是同样的东西：眼前这段路找不找得到、值不值得把船带进去冒险。海洋营的不同在于，这一次他把等待写成了一个计划：营地选在更结实的浮冰上，理由里挂着一个具体的指望——附近可能开出水道，那时可以划船去找陆地——等条件更有利，再做第二次尝试。

One reading, and it is the author's, is that Ocean Camp was not the first time he chose to stop. On the march's second morning, with snow too thick to see a path, he decided not to strike camp; when it cleared and a good floe turned up, they moved on after lunch. Both decisions weighed the same things: could a road be found, and was it worth taking the boats into danger to use it? What set Ocean Camp apart is that this time he wrote the waiting down as a plan. The camp went onto a more solid floe, the reasoning carried a specific hope (leads opening nearby, boats in the water, land to the north-west), and a second attempt was to follow once conditions improved.
还有一处值得注意（作者的解读）：停下之后，他们反而能一趟趟回到沉船附近，捞回衣物、食物和少数私人物品；沙克尔顿后来说，那些私人物品当初是怀着“轻松的乐观”，才打算在冲过移动冰面奔向安全时丢在几英里之外的。他们还决定几乎全靠海豹和企鹅过活，把雪橇口粮留给后面的小艇航行。作者认为，停下不只是不再消耗，也是把资源重新收拢的时间。

One more thing is worth noticing, and again it is the author's reading. Once they stopped, they could go back to the wreck again and again and retrieve clothing, food and some few articles of personal value; Shackleton later said it was in "light-hearted optimism" that they had thought to leave those articles miles behind on their dash across the moving ice to safety. They also chose to live almost entirely on seals and penguins so that the sledging rations could be kept for the boat journey ahead. On this reading, stopping was not only a halt to the drain; it was time to gather their resources again.
另一种解释是关于取舍的标准（作者推断）：金币被扔掉、照片被留下，他在这几段里没有说明原因；扉页则被他撕了下来，这段记述没有写它的去向。作者的推测是：在冰上，金币和照片都换不来什么，但照片被留下了。也许那道上限筛的只是重量，也许只是个人偏好，两种说法都超出了他写下的内容。

A second reading, and it is the author's, concerns the standard behind the choices. The sovereigns were thrown away and the photographs were kept, and he gives no reason in these passages; the fly-leaf was torn out, and the passage does not say what became of it. The author's guess is that on the ice neither the gold coins nor the photographs could buy anything, yet the photographs were kept. Perhaps the limit screened only for weight; perhaps it was personal preference. Both go beyond what he wrote.
场景一：一个创业团队的融资没谈成，原计划已经不成立。负责人第一次全员会上最有用的，也许就是像本文开头那个一句话的新任务一样，用一句话说清新的目标：现在要做到什么，怎么算做到。

Scenario one: a start-up's fundraising has fallen through and the original plan no longer stands. At the first all-hands meeting, the most useful thing the founder can do may be what the new task at the start of this piece did: state the new goal in one sentence, what has to be achieved now and how you will know.

dispositions.rationale: 英文的船名 Endurance 改为 the ship。证据中没有船名，改后与中文一致；中文原文照录，没有改动。
删去英文中“a base on the far side of the continent”整句。证据只写了 Ross Sea base，中文也没有这句。

evidence.quote: reaching the Ross Sea base in five months

dispositions.rationale: 「同时定下规矩」/At the same time 改为「他还定下规矩」/He also fixed the rule。证据没有说明这条命令下达的时间。

evidence.quote: The order was that personal gear must not exceed two pounds per man

dispositions.rationale: 「用他的原话」改为「照他的说法」，表明后面是转述，不是逐字原文。英文也相应改为 As he put it。

evidence.quote: We could not afford to cumber ourselves with unnecessary weight.

dispositions.rationale: 删去「外衣」和“— Burberry coats —”的释义，只保留证据原词 Burberrys。

evidence.quote: a complete new set of Burberrys and underclothing

dispositions.rationale: 「下午开路顺利得多」改为「开路时有过顺利的时候」/At one stage the work went well。不再写具体时段，也不与此前作比较。
改为「他记下挪动两条船的艰难」/He recorded how hard it was to shift the two boats，不再把这次搬运指认为搬往海洋营。

evidence.quote: It was with the utmost difficulty that we shifted our two boats.

dispositions.rationale: 删去「扎营后」/Once in camp，改为「他还决定」/He also decided；英文引文从 to conserve 开始，与证据逐字一致。

evidence.quote: I decided to conserve our valuable sledging rations

dispositions.rationale: 顺序改为先天晴、探到浮冰，午饭后才继续走，删去“午后天晴”的说法。

evidence.quote: Then, as the weather cleared, Worsley and I made a prospect to the west

dispositions.rationale: 「轻松的乐观」改为只修饰当初打算丢下私人物品这件事，不再写成对整个冲刺计划的评语。

evidence.quote: which in our light-hearted optimism we had thought to leave miles behind us on our dash across the moving ice to safety

dispositions.rationale: 末句的“在这份记述里/In his account”改为「作者认为」/On this reading，明确这是作者的解读。
首句改为先陈述弃留事实，说明他没有给出原因，再把“换不来什么”明确标为作者的推测。

evidence.quote: So sovereigns were thrown away and photographs were kept.

dispositions.rationale: 不再把扉页算作被留下：改为扉页被撕下，记述没有写它的去向。

evidence.quote: I tore the fly-leaf out of the Bible that Queen Alexandra had given to the ship

dispositions.rationale: 删去现代场景中的证据引句，改为「像本文开头那个一句话的新任务一样」/what the new task at the start of this piece did。
与 F12 是同一问题，已在 analysis.2 的同一处改写中修正：首句只陈述弃留，理由标为作者推测。

evidence.quote: So sovereigns were thrown away and photographs were kept.
